bottom_line: Anifrolumab — TULIP-1. Stated failure: Phase III: SRI-4 primary endpoint missed. Diagnosis (claim 1.2, supported): The primary analysis missed the endpoint: mean difference -4.2 (95% CI -14.2 to 5.8), p=0.412, favoring neither group convincingly.
lines: [1] TULIP-1's prespecified primary endpoint was SRI-4 at Week 52 under original restricted medication rules. (section: Failure Diagnosis; sources: ClinicalTrials.gov; record types: registry; evidence status: prespecified; evidence strength: strong; check: supported by its cited records).

[2] The primary analysis missed the endpoint: mean difference -4.2 (95% CI -14.2 to 5.8), p=0.412, favoring neither group convincingly. (section: Failure Diagnosis; sources: ClinicalTrials.gov; record types: registry; evidence status: prespecified; evidence strength: strong; check: supported by its cited records).

[3] The curated record states TULIP-1 missed SRI-4, a composite lupus response measure. (section: Failure Diagnosis; sources: curated record; record types: curated; evidence status: curated summary; evidence strength: strong; check: supported by its cited records).

[4] Post-hoc SRI-4 analyses with revised restricted medication rules at Week 52 also failed: mean difference 3.9 (95% CI -6.3 to 14.1), p=0.455. (section: Failure Diagnosis; sources: ClinicalTrials.gov; record types: registry; evidence status: post hoc; evidence strength: strong; check: hypothesis-generating).

[5] Post-hoc SRI-4 at Week 24 with revised rules also failed: mean difference 3.3 (95% CI -6.7 to 13.4), p=0.515. (section: Failure Diagnosis; sources: ClinicalTrials.gov; record types: registry; evidence status: post hoc; evidence strength: strong; check: hypothesis-generating).

[6] Post-hoc BICLA at Week 52 with revised rules appeared favorable: mean difference 16.4 (95% CI 6.7 to 26.2), p not reported. (section: Failure Diagnosis; sources: ClinicalTrials.gov; record types: registry; evidence status: post hoc; evidence strength: strong; check: hypothesis-generating).

[7] Prespecified BICLA at Week 52 with original rules showed mean difference 10.1 (95% CI 0.6 to 19.7), p not reported. (section: Failure Diagnosis; sources: ClinicalTrials.gov; record types: registry; evidence status: prespecified; evidence strength: strong; check: supported by its cited records).

[8] After failure, AstraZeneca pivoted to BICLA for TULIP-2 because evaluation showed a more favorable response using BICLA, an alternative measure already collected in the program. (section: Failure Diagnosis; sources: curated record; record types: curated; evidence status: curated summary; evidence strength: strong; check: supported by its cited records).

[9] TULIP-2 succeeded and Saphnelo received US approval in 2021; this confirms a revised endpoint in another trial, not retroactively converting TULIP-1 into a success. (section: Failure Diagnosis; sources: curated record; record types: curated; evidence status: curated summary; evidence strength: strong; check: supported by its cited records).

[10] TULIP-1's prespecified primary endpoint was SRI-4 at Week 52 under original restricted medication rules; the anifrolumab vs placebo mean difference was -4.2 (95% CI -14.2 to 5.8, p=0.412), so it missed the primary endpoint. (section: Candidate Responder Population; sources: ClinicalTrials.gov; record types: registry; evidence status: prespecified; evidence strength: strong; check: supported by its cited records).

[11] Post-hoc analyses with revised restricted medication rules did not rescue SRI-4 at Week 52 (mean difference 3.9, 95% CI -6.3 to 14.1, p=0.455) or at Week 24 (mean difference 3.3, 95% CI -6.7 to 13.4, p=0.515). (section: Candidate Responder Population; sources: ClinicalTrials.gov; record types: registry; evidence status: post hoc; evidence strength: strong; check: hypothesis-generating).

[12] A post-hoc BICLA analysis with revised restricted medication rules at Week 52 showed a more favorable response (mean difference 16.4, 95% CI 6.7 to 26.2), supporting BICLA as an alternative endpoint already collected in the program. (section: Candidate Responder Population; sources: ClinicalTrials.gov; record types: registry; evidence status: post hoc; evidence strength: strong; check: hypothesis-generating).

[13] After TULIP-1 failed SRI-4, AstraZeneca chose BICLA for TULIP-2; TULIP-2 succeeded and Saphnelo received US approval in 2021, confirming the revised endpoint in another trial rather than retroactively converting TULIP-1 into a success. (section: Candidate Responder Population; sources: curated record; record types: curated; evidence status: curated summary; evidence strength: strong; check: supported by its cited records).

[14] TULIP-1 (NCT02446912) studied anifrolumab in systemic lupus erythematosus. (section: Related Indications; sources: curated record, ClinicalTrials.gov; record types: curator confirmed, registry; evidence status: registry record; evidence strength: strong; check: supported by its cited records).

[15] TULIP-1's prespecified primary endpoint was SRI-4 at Week 52 under original restricted medication rules, and it missed: mean difference -4.2 (95% CI -14.2 to 5.8, p=0.412) and -2.6 (95% CI -14.7 to 9.6). (section: Evidence-Supported Redesign Options; sources: ClinicalTrials.gov; record types: registry; evidence status: prespecified; evidence strength: strong; check: supported by its cited records).

[16] In TULIP-1 post-hoc analyses with revised restricted medication rules, SRI-4 mean difference at Week 52 was 3.9 (95% CI -6.3 to 14.1, p=0.455), at Week 24 was 3.3 (95% CI -6.7 to 13.4, p=0.515), and in the IFN-high subgroup at Week 52 was 6.4 (95% CI -4.8 to 17.7, p=0.261). (section: Evidence-Supported Redesign Options; sources: ClinicalTrials.gov; record types: registry; evidence status: post hoc; evidence strength: strong; check: hypothesis-generating).

[17] BICLA was a secondary endpoint in TULIP-1; original analysis showed mean difference 10.1 (95% CI 0.6 to 19.7) favoring anifrolumab, and post-hoc analysis with revised rules showed mean difference 16.4 (95% CI 6.7 to 26.2). (section: Evidence-Supported Redesign Options; sources: ClinicalTrials.gov; record types: registry; evidence status: post hoc; evidence strength: strong; check: hypothesis-generating).

[18] After TULIP-1 failed, AstraZeneca pivoted to BICLA as the primary endpoint for TULIP-2 because evaluation showed a more favorable response using BICLA, an alternative measure already collected in the program; TULIP-2 succeeded and Saphnelo received US approval in 2021. (section: Evidence-Supported Redesign Options; sources: curated record; record types: curated; evidence status: curated summary; evidence strength: strong; check: supported by its cited records).

[19] The TULIP-2 success prospectively confirmed BICLA as an effective endpoint for anifrolumab in a new confirmatory trial, but this did not retroactively convert TULIP-1 into a success. (section: Evidence-Supported Redesign Options; sources: curated record; record types: curated; evidence status: prospectively confirmed; evidence strength: strong; check: supported by its cited records).
question: Why did TULIP-1 miss its primary endpoint, and what changed later?
raw: TULIP-1 missed its prespecified primary endpoint of SRI-4 at Week 52 under original restricted medication rules, with a mean difference of -4.2 (95% CI -14.2 to 5.8, p=0.412) [1][2][10]. Post-hoc analyses with revised rules did not rescue SRI-4 at Week 52 or Week 24 [4][5][11]. However, post-hoc BICLA analyses showed more favorable responses [6][12], and prespecified BICLA results favored anifrolumab [7]. Based on these curated summaries, AstraZeneca pivoted to BICLA for TULIP-2, which succeeded and led to US approval [8][9][13][18][19]. The lines do not show that TULIP-1 was retroactively converted into a success [9][13][19].
